name: Balwoo Gongyang
summary: Buddhist temple-food courses opposite Jogyesa — calm, vegan, seasonal and gentle on the stomach.
description: Run by the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, Balwoo Gongyang serves temple cuisine: no meat, fish, garlic or onion, relying instead on mountain greens, fermented jang and seasonal produce. Courses range from a weekday-lunch Seon-sik set to the pre-booked Hui-sik feast. The fifth-floor rooms overlook Jogyesa Temple and feel serene after Insadong's crowds. It held a Michelin star for several years but is not listed among the 2026 starred restaurants.
tips: Weekday lunch Seon-sik is the best value; Hui-sik (₩120,000) needs advance booking.
Naver reviewers bring parents for a healthy, mild meal.
Closed Sundays and 24–26 Sep (Chuseok).
Anguk Station Exit 6, ~5 minutes; combine with Insadong and Jogyesa.

reviews.text: Many praise the gourmet vegan temple food, presentation and service; a minority found some dishes bland or cold.

name: Bao Seoul Seongsu
summary: Taiwanese gua bao and beef noodle soup on Seongsu’s Yeonmujang-gil — a Taipei-street feel in a sleek red room.
description: Bao Seoul brings Taipei street food to Seongsu’s main food lane: pillowy gua bao stuffed with braised pork, lamb, prawn or chicken katsu, plus Taiwanese beef noodle soup, beef-tripe noodles and cold peanut noodles. Naver reviewers say it tastes like being back in Taiwan and rate the room highly. It is a known queue spot among young Seoulites but rarely on foreign visitors’ lists. Combine it with Seongsu’s flagship stores and pop-ups.
tips: Closed 24–25 Sep; open 26 Sep with holiday hours (Naver).
Arrive just before 17:00 or on a weekday to skip the usual queue.
Order bao for the table plus two bowls of noodles to share.

reviews.text: Usually a long queue, but arriving just before dinner meant walking straight in; the food was excellent.
“So good it made me want to go back to Taiwan” — the classic bao was soft and tasted just like Taipei.
EatingSeoul describes a fast-casual bao specialist that has become a fixture of Seongsu’s Yeonmujang-gil food street.

name: Bicena
summary: Michelin-star Korean tasting menus on the 81st floor of Lotte World Tower — the most dramatic dining view in Seoul.
description: Bicena sits on the 81st floor of Lotte World Tower, Korea's tallest building, with floor-to-ceiling views over the Han River and Jamsil. The cooking is refined Korean with a Gyeongsang-do accent: house-dry-aged hanwoo sirloin, pork belly and seasonal banchan served on beautiful ceramics. It holds one Michelin star in 2026. Combine it with Seoul Sky or the Lotte World Mall below for a futuristic Jamsil day.
tips: Lunch Sancheon course ₩170,000 (weekday/weekend/holiday) vs dinner ₩280,000 (Naver menu, 2026).
Book a window table at sunset for day-to-night views.
Owner-set Chuseok hours on Naver: open 12:30–22:00 on 24–26 Sep.

name: Bongsanok
summary: North Korean Hwanghae-style dumpling soup and squid sundae in a quiet alley 5 minutes from home.
description: Bongsanok cooks Hwanghae-province (North Korean) home food: generous, mild dumpling soup, stuffed-squid sundae, mung-bean pancakes and chilled kimchi-mari noodles. The flavours are gentle and clean rather than fiery, which regulars describe as healthy. It is tucked in a side street by Nambu Bus Terminal, practically on the family's doorstep. A good light lunch with parents.

name: Born & Bred
summary: Hanwoo beef omakase from a Majang-dong butcher family: four floors, staff-grilled cuts, private rooms
description: Born & Bred grew out of a hanwoo wholesaler that has traded beef in the Majang-dong meat market since 1978, and it claims Korea's first hanwoo omakase. The new building has a different concept on each floor. The basement Speakeasy serves the full omakase at one 19:00 seating, the 2F hall has à la carte cuts and a casual tasting menu, and 3F has private rooms serving a shorter 13–14-course menu. Staff grill every cut at the table and explain it. The room is polished, with marble counters, copper grills and a butcher case by the door. It is listed in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide and appeared on Asia's 50 Best Restaurants' extended 51–100 list in 2024.
highlights: 2F casual tasting menu with yukhoe (beef tartare) and a mixed beef platter
Brisket hot-pot rice with soybean-paste soup
tips: For five people, book a 3F private room on CatchTable. Lunch there costs ₩230,000 per person, less than dinner (₩280,000).
The 2F hall is the cheaper way in: a 200 g hanwoo platter is ₩100,000 and staff still grill it for you.
Majang Station (Line 5) Exit 3 is a 4-minute walk. You pass the huge Majang meat market on the way.
Closed Tuesdays. The break is 15:00–18:00 and last order is 21:15. Corkage is free for one bottle per person.

name: Brooklyn The Burger Joint (Seorae)
summary: Seorae Village’s original American burger joint: fresh-ground patties, stacked cheeseburgers and thick shakes near home.
description: Brooklyn The Burger Joint is Seorae Village’s long-running American burger bar, and it grinds its certified beef fresh daily. TripAdvisor rates it 4.5 and among the top 100 restaurants in Seoul. Naver diners say even parents enjoyed the juicy patties.

name: Buchon Yukhoe
summary: Gwangjang Market's famous beef-tartare house: silky yukhoe with pear and egg yolk, and cheap yukhoe bibimbap.
description: Buchon Yukhoe sits in the yukhoe alley of Gwangjang Market and has become one of the market's best-known restaurants. Fresh beef is hand-sliced and dressed with sesame oil and pear, crowned with egg yolk; yukhoe bibimbap is the budget way in. It has appeared in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul and is now hugely popular with foreign visitors. A proper indoor restaurant, it is more comfortable for parents than the market's stall benches.
tips: Register on the CatchTable waitlist; a Saturday-evening visitor faced ~50 teams ahead (Sept 2026).

name: Byeokje Galbi (Bangi flagship)
summary: Seoul's blue-chip hanwoo galbi house: top-grade marbled short rib and ribeye, plus classic Pyongyang naengmyeon
description: Byeokje Galbi has served hanwoo short ribs since 1986, and Korean families book the Bangi-dong flagship near Olympic Park for big celebrations. It buys only top-grade cattle (BMS No. 9) at auction, and in-house butchers cut the beef. The signatures are the 'Seolhwa' diamond-cut saeng-galbi (short rib) and kkot-deungsim (ribeye), grilled for you over charcoal. There is also a serious Pyongyang-style naengmyeon and hanwoo soups for lighter eaters. Staff are formal, the dining rooms are hushed, and upstairs rooms suit a family of five. VisitKorea notes its recognition in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul 2023.
highlights: Seolhwa saeng-galbi (diamond-cut hanwoo short rib), 200 g ₩160,000
Seolhwa galbi-tang or oxtail soup lunch sets
tips: Lunch (11:30–15:00) is the smart way in. A 120 g sirloin set costs ₩69,000 and a mixed-cut set ₩59,000 (minimum two people). Soup and naengmyeon trays are ₩35,000–45,000.
Book on CatchTable and ask for a 2F private room for five.
Bangi Station (Line 5) Exit 4 is a 3-minute walk. Pair it with a walk in Olympic Park or a trip to Lotte World Tower.
On TripAdvisor, a few foreign diners complain of rushed service at peak dinner times. Go at a quieter lunch or early-evening slot.

summary: Calm hanjeongsik courses by Gyodae — where Seocho families hold formal meals; lunch courses from ₩35,000.

name: Daedo Sikdang (Wangsimni main)
summary: Hanwoo sirloin on cast-iron since 1964 — Seoul's classic beef house, finished with legendary kkakdugi fried rice.
description: Daedo Sikdang has been grilling thick-cut hanwoo sirloin on heavy iron plates in Wangsimni since 1964, and the main branch is still where Seoulites take their parents for a beef night. The menu is short: sirloin, a few special cuts, and kkakdugi (radish kimchi) fried rice made in the beef fat at the end. The main store has been refreshed and expanded into annex buildings, and Naver reviewers mention good ventilation and a spacious room. Prices are high but well below Cheongdam steak houses for comparable hanwoo.
tips: Private rooms seat 4–12 (Naver seating info) — request one for a family of five.
Always leave room for the kkakdugi fried rice (₩6,000); regulars consider it the point of the meal.
Valet and paid parking available; by subway use Sangwangsimni Exit 2 (≈6 min) or Wangsimni.
Recent reviewers note grilling can be self-service at busy times — ask staff to help.

Returning diners say the renovated main store and new annex buildings feel clean and pleasant, and the meat is as good as ever.

name: Damtaek
summary: Bib Gourmand shio ramen near Hapjeong: clear, delicate chicken-seafood broth with a bright yuzu version.
description: Damtaek is a small, minimalist ramen shop on a Seogyo-dong side street that the Michelin Guide lists as a Bib Gourmand. Its speciality is shio (salt) ramen — a clear, gently sweet broth with tender chashu — plus yuzu shio, wasabi and prawn versions and a neungi-mushroom mazemen. Naver diners praise the chewy noodles and free extra rice or noodles. It is far less known to foreign visitors than Oreno, a 10-minute walk away.

summary: Taipei’s famous xiaolongbao house by Gangnam Station — spacious, fast and reliable, 15 minutes from home.
description: The Gangnam branch of the Taiwanese chain occupies a large second-floor room by Gangnam Station, so families rarely wait long. Xiaolongbao come in classic pork, crab, shrimp, chicken, pine mushroom and truffle versions, alongside shrimp shaomai, beef noodle soup and fried rice. Naver diners praise the spacious room, quick service and kind staff; TripAdvisor reviewers are split between “best dim sum in Seoul” and fans of other branches. It is a dependable, parent-friendly lunch near home.

name: Doughroom
summary: Chef Lee Jun’s fresh-pasta Italian in Bangbae: squid-ink capellini, lobster ravioli and scallops, near home.
description: Doughroom is the Italian restaurant of chef Lee Jun (of two-Michelin-star Soigné), who appeared on Netflix’s Culinary Class Wars season 2, according to Naver diners. The focus is fresh pasta — squid-ink capellini in butter sauce with prawns, lobster ravioli, potato gnocchi — plus Caesar salad, scallops and duck. It is listed in the Michelin Guide Seoul and is a 10-minute taxi from home. Naver reviewers use it for children’s birthdays and couples’ dinners.

name: Eatanic Garden (Josun Palace)
summary: Michelin-star 'urban garden' tasting menu 36 floors above Gangnam — the closest star to home, with sweeping city views.
description: Eatanic Garden occupies the 36th floor of Josun Palace in Yeoksam, a few Line 2 stops from home. Chef Son Jong-won builds each seasonal course around one Korean ingredient, introduced with an illustrated card, and plates it with a strong visual identity. Window tables look over Gangnam's towers, especially dramatic after dark. It holds one Michelin star in 2026 and appeared on Asia's 50 Best Restaurants 2024 (#62, extended list).

Closed Mondays and Tuesdays — 28–29 Sep won't work.

name: ELPIC
summary: Michelin-listed Cheongdam grill pairing wood-fired steak with Jeju seafood: tartare, ceviche, octopus-barley risotto.
description: ELPIC is a compact, concrete-and-stone grill room on a Cheongdam side street, listed in the Michelin Guide Seoul. The menu is sharing-style: beef tartare on crisps, seasonal Jeju fish ceviche, octopus with barley risotto, grilled abalone in brown butter, quail, sweet-shrimp bisque pasta and steaks from the grill. Naver diners call the steak superb and the owner and staff warm and fun, and many bring their own wine. It stays mostly under foreign visitors’ radar.
tips: Dinner only Tue–Thu, lunch and dinner Fri–Sat, lunch only Sun, closed Mon (Naver).
No 2026 Chuseok notice — call ahead for 24–26 Sep.
Order 4–5 plates plus one steak to share among five.

reviews.text: Listed in the Michelin Guide Seoul selection.
The steak needs no words; the octopus was excellent and the owner and staff are kind and fun.
Meat was grilled to bring out its flavour and matched well with the wine the diner brought; a relaxed pace.

name: Escondido
summary: Asia’s first Michelin-starred Mexican restaurant: chef Jin Woo-bum’s tortilla-and-mole tasting menu in a hidden Hannam basement.
description: Escondido (“hidden”) sits in a Hannam-dong alley basement behind an unmarked door, with a warm, dim counter room. Chef Jin Woo-bum’s dinner-only tasting menu is built around tortillas, moles and salsas, with cocktail pairings available. The Michelin Guide 2026 lists it with one star — the Guide has called it Asia’s first Michelin-starred Mexican restaurant. Naver diners describe beautifully coloured, precise plates.
tips: Dinner only from 17:15, Tue–Sat; closed 25–26 Sep and every Sunday and Monday (Naver).
Counter seating is intimate — request five seats together on CatchTable.
The alley entrance is easy to miss: look for the small lit sign.

reviews.text: The Michelin Guide describes bona fide Mexican cuisine with the chef’s twists, making nuanced use of tortilla and mole.
A first-timer says every course from the appetiser on was neat and beautifully coloured.
Crisp, spicy and fragrant spice notes all came through, and the paired cocktails were excellent.

name: Eulmildae
summary: One of Seoul's 'big four' Pyongyang naengmyeon houses — slushy-cold broth, thick buckwheat noodles and mung-bean jeon.
description: Eulmildae in Yeomni-dong is counted by Korean noodle fans among Seoul's four great Pyongyang naengmyeon houses. Its broth is served ice-slushy with a bolder flavour than Woo Lae Oak, and regulars order 'georaeng' (no ice) or 'yang manhi' (extra noodles) by code. Suyuk (boiled beef) and nokdu-jeon (mung-bean pancake) make it a proper meal. It is a busy, no-frills local institution rather than a polished dining room.
tips: Order like a regular: 'georaeng' = broth without the ice slush, 'yang manhi' = extra noodles.
Queues move fast; there is a shaded waiting area. Rainy days mean shorter lines (Naver reviewers).
Closed the whole Chuseok break — go 23 Sep or from 28 Sep.
Daeheung Station Exit 2, about 6 minutes on foot.

reviews.text: Reviewers call it authentic Pyongyang-style naengmyeon with great noodle texture and finely crushed ice; locals queue even before noon.
Visited one of Seoul's four great Pyongyang naengmyeon houses and found it lived up to its reputation (Sept 2026).
Waited about 15 minutes at 12:30 on a Friday; shade and cool air at the queue made it bearable.

name: Farno Seorae
summary: Seorae Village all-day brunch spot near home: daily soups, hummus, omelettes and lasagne from 8 a.m., no break time.
description: Farno is a small, calm all-day kitchen on a Seorae Village side street, a short taxi ride from home. It opens at 8:00 with an early-bird breakfast set, then serves a rotating daily soup with toast, quinoa-mushroom and Cobb salads, hummus, vegetable omelettes, shakshuka-style eggs and lasagne through to 20:00 without a break. Naver regulars call it their favourite Seorae brunch for its atmosphere and friendly staff. It is little known outside the neighbourhood.
tips: Open daily 08:00–20:00 with no break — easy breakfast before a day out.

summary: Michelin Bib soy-marinated crab set meals in a sleek, design-led room — the stylish way to try gejang in Gangnam.
description: Gebangsikdang was started by a fashion marketer and his parents, long-time gejang restaurateurs, and it shows: a polished, minimalist dining room with neat trays of banchan. Flavours are clean and not too salty. It holds a Bib Gourmand in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul 2026.
tips: Crab-flesh-and-roe rice bowls avoid messy shells — good for parents.

name: Geumdwaeji Sikdang (Gold Pig)
summary: Michelin Bib pork BBQ in Yaksu: thick YBD pork belly grilled by staff, wrapped in grilled basil — worth the famous queue.
description: Gold Pig is often named among Seoul's top three pork houses and holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand. It uses YBD crossbreed pork — thick 'bon-samgyeop' belly and snowflake-marbled neck — grilled for you over charcoal and served with a signature grilled-basil wrap. Staff scrub the grill and extractor between parties, so the three-storey building stays cleaner than a typical pork joint. The whole-pig kimchi jjigae is a cult side order.
tips: No bookings: register on the CatchTable on-site waitlist from about 10:00; a Sept 2026 reviewer got #25 at 10:00 and was seated ~11:45.
Upper floors open later — choose 'first available' floor to be seated faster.
Yaksu Station Exit 2, about 4 minutes on foot.
The ground floor is bar-style; ask for a table if the group of five wants to sit together.

description: Gigas occupies a bright, pale-wood room on the third floor of Piknic, the art space on Namsan’s lower slope near Hoehyeon. summary: Massimo Bottura’s Gucci Osteria in Cheongdam: playful Italian tasting menus on Gucci tableware in a green, jewel-box room.
description: Gucci Osteria, created with three-Michelin-star chef Massimo Bottura, moved from Itaewon to the fifth floor of Gucci’s Cheongdam flagship in 2025. The room is calm green with Gucci-patterned porcelain, and the tasting menus riff on Italian classics such as ragù, fresh pasta and gnocchi. It holds a place in the Michelin Guide Seoul. Naver diners praise the courses and wine service; one TripAdvisor reviewer found some dishes under-seasoned.
tips: Open through Chuseok with regular hours on 24–26 Sep (Naver); Sunday lunch only, closed Mondays.
Browse the Gucci flagship below before or after.
Book the private room for five on CatchTable.

reviews.text: One reviewer found flavours lacking depth and some dishes under-seasoned, expecting more creativity from Bottura’s name.
A diner who ate in the private room found the course well built, with strongly Italian flavours.
A returning guest says the new location feels very different from Hannam — ragù, pasta and gnocchi were all excellent.

name: Gyodae Ijeung Jip (main)
summary: Gyodae's beloved 'second-floor house': flower-cut pork belly grilled for you, 12 minutes' walk from home.
description: Ijeung Jip ('the second-floor house') has been a Gyodae office-worker favourite for more than a decade, and the main branch is a short walk from home. The signature kkot-samgyeop is pork belly scored into a flower pattern so it crisps evenly, grilled by staff and wrapped with scallion salad, pickled chilli and a dab of myeongnan. Rooms seat 6–9 and group areas are spacious, so five fit comfortably. Hanwoo doenjang stew and fried rice finish the meal.
tips: Hidden gem: 2,600+ Naver reviews, almost no foreign reviews — it's where Seocho locals go.
Private rooms seat 6–9 — book one via Naver for the family.
Corkage-free according to Kakao tags — bring a bottle of wine.
Open until 00:30 (23:00 on 25 Sep); Gyodae Station Exit 14, 2 minutes.

reviews.text: The flower-cut pork belly is as pretty as its name and melt-soft; wrapped with scallion, pickled chilli and a bit of myeongnan it was superb (Jul 2026).
Gyodae's go-to pork place — roomy seating and fun, unusual tables (Sept 2026).
Side dishes, pork belly and the steamed egg all praised; heard the main branch beats the others and agreed (Apr 2026).

name: Hadongkwan
summary: Clear brass-bowl gomtang since 1939 — Myeongdong's breakfast beef soup that closes when the pot runs dry.
description: Hadongkwan has served one dish, gomtang, since 1939: a clear, deeply savoury beef broth with brisket (and tripe if you like) over rice, served in brass bowls. You pay first, choose your size, add scallions and the Seoul-style kkakdugi, and eat quickly among office workers. It opens at 07:00, making it one of the best early breakfasts in central Seoul. It appears in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul 2026.
tips: Go for breakfast (07:00–09:00) to avoid the lunch rush and catch the freshest pot.
Pay at the counter first; ₩18,000 is meat-only, ₩25,000 adds offal ('naejang manhi' for extra).
Regulars add lots of scallion and skip pepper at first to taste the broth.
Closed Sundays; closes at 16:00 or earlier if sold out.

tripadvisor.rank: #315 of 19,343 Restaurants in Seoul

reviews.text: Came at 08:00 on a weekday for a hangover breakfast — quiet, and the basic gomtang was clean and comforting (Aug 2026).
Prepaid ₩25,000 bowl with extra offal; prefers this clear brisket-style broth to milky versions (Aug 2026).
Opinions split: fans call it authentic traditional gomtang, while some visitors found the old-school experience underwhelming for the price.

hours.note: Closes earlier when the soup sells out; closed Sundays.

name: Haidilao Hot Pot Seocho (Gangnam)
summary: Famous-service Chinese hot pot by Sinnonhyeon, open until 7 a.m.: pick your broths, spice level and a DIY sauce bar.
description: Haidilao is the Chinese hot-pot chain known for over-the-top hospitality, and its Seocho branch sits one minute from Sinnonhyeon Station in the Gangnam Station district. Split pots let a family combine mild tomato or mushroom broth with fiery mala, and there is a large DIY sauce bar. Staff often speak Chinese and some English, and TripAdvisor reviewers highlight fast service. It is open 10:00–07:00 daily, useful for late dinners.
highlights: Lu rou fan and youtiao sides
tips: Queues are long at dinner — a Naver diner waited 75 minutes from 17:30; weekday 11:00 is almost walk-in.
Tables have a 90-minute limit at busy times.
One minute from Sinnonhyeon Exit 7; about 15 minutes from home by taxi.

reviews.text: Reviewers highlight attentive Haidilao-style hospitality, fast service and customisable spicy broths.
A five-time visitor to this branch says arriving around 11 a.m. on a weekday meant almost no wait.
A diner queued from 17:30 to 18:45 on a Tuesday but says the rich tomato broth and service are always worth it.

name: Hanilkwan Apgujeong
summary: Seoul's grande dame of Korean cooking since 1939 — bulgogi, galbitang and Seoul naengmyeon in a calm Apgujeong house.
description: Hanilkwan opened in Jongno in 1939 and is one of Seoul's oldest restaurant names; its Apgujeong flagship is where three-generation families gather for bulgogi, galbitang and Seoul-style cold noodles. The menu is broad and gentle rather than fiery, which suits parents and first-timers alike. Dishes are neat and mild, service is polished, and valet parking makes it an easy family dinner stop. It is about three stops from home on Line 3.
tips: Lunch sets (bulgogi ₩39,000 / galbi ₩49,000) are the easiest way to try the classics.
Naver reviewers call it ideal for dining with parents — mild, clean flavours and quiet rooms.
Valet parking available; Apgujeong Station Exit 2, about 5 minutes on foot.
Galbitang (₩20,000) plus a shared bindaetteok makes a lighter, cheaper meal.

reviews.text: Galbitang was hot and hearty, the royal bibimbap mild and clean — a good place to eat with parents (Sept 2026 visitor).
Tastes like home! Clean spot, kind service, and so many dishes to choose from. Valet parking available too
A regular loves the galbi set, goldongban, mung-bean jelly, bindaetteok and jellyfish salad, and always adds pan-fried dumplings.

price.note: Galbitang ₩20,000; Seoul naengmyeon ₩14,000; lunch set bulgogi ₩39,000 / galbi ₩49,000 (Naver menu, 2026)

name: Horapa
summary: Bib Gourmand Thai in Seochon from a chef trained at nahm: bold southern curries, grilled kai kolae and fiery salads.
description: Chef Son Seung-hee trained at Bangkok’s nahm before opening Horapa on the second floor of a Seochon building near Gyeongbokgung. The menu goes well beyond pad thai: crisp fried pork head with house sriracha, massaman with pork ribs, jungle curry, green papaya som tam and the pre-order kai kolae (southern Thai grilled chicken). Naver diners praise authentic spicing, friendly explanations of every dish and good wine pairings. It is a Michelin Bib Gourmand.
tips: Closed 25–26 Sep and every Sunday and Monday; open Thu 24 Sep 10:00–22:00 (Naver).
Pre-order the kai kolae when booking on CatchTable.
Pair with Gyeongbokgung (closed Tuesdays) or Seochon’s galleries.

reviews.text: The Michelin Guide lists Horapa as a Bib Gourmand for good-quality, good-value Thai cooking.
A first-time diner calls it the best Thai food they’ve had — every dish distinctive, great with wine, staff kind.
The pre-order kai kolae is a must: moist chicken with a gently curried sauce to dip in soft yolk.

summary: Michelin Bib beef-bone kalguksu and giant handmade mandu on the Samcheong-dong road near Gyeongbokgung.
description: Hwangsaengga is a Bukchon favourite for soft hand-cut noodles in a milky beef-bone broth and fist-sized dumplings stuffed with pork, tofu and vegetables. The menu also includes kongguksu in season, bossam and mushroom hot pot for sharing. It sits on the stroll between Gyeongbokgung, Bukchon and Samcheong-dong, making a comforting lunch stop for parents. Listed as a Bib Gourmand in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul 2026.
tips: Queues can be very long at lunch; weekday late lunch often has no wait (Aug 2026 Naver review).
Order one plate of wang mandu per two people to share.
Anguk Station Exit 1 is ~11 min; easier to walk from Gyeongbokgung's east gate.
Closed Chuseok day (25 Sep) only.

Walking to Samcheong-dong on an autumn day, spotted a short queue at the usually packed shop and jumped in (Sept 2026).

name: Hyodo Chicken (Express Bus Terminal)
summary: Chef-created Korean fried chicken with blistered shishito and anchovies — a roomy branch 5 minutes from home.
description: Hyodo Chicken's recipes were developed with Mingles chef Kang Min-goo, which explains ideas like soy-glazed chicken tossed with blistered kkwari peppers and crisp anchovies, or 'Go-ma-wo' chicken with lotus root and garlic. The Express Bus Terminal branch is one of the most spacious, and Naver reviewers single it out for its roomy, comfortable space. It is the easiest casual dinner near home — chicken, beer and zero planning.
tips: Near home: Express Bus Terminal Station Exit 1, ~4 minutes; a short taxi from Seocho.
Naver reviewers praise this branch for being spacious — easy for five.
Order one signature plus a plain crispy for anyone who dislikes spice.
Open until 23:00 (LO 22:00) — good after a late shopping run at Shinsegae.

reviews.text: The Express Bus Terminal branch is special because the space is so roomy and comfortable (Aug 2026).
The shishito-pepper chicken lived up to the hype; great for families — the boneless chicken ordered for the kids vanished (Aug 2026).
At the original branch, reviewers praise the varieties, chicken-and-beer pairing and friendly staff.

name: Hyotteu
summary: Yongnidan-gil’s famous Vietnamese spot: clear beef pho, bún chả bowls and wok-fired rice in a Saigon-street room.
description: Hyotteu helped turn Yongnidan-gil near Sinyongsan Station into one of Seoul’s buzziest dining streets. The room feels like a Vietnamese street stall, and the menu covers light beef pho, spicy beef pho, bún chả rice-noodle bowls, seafood egg noodles and smoky fried rice. English-language guides describe the food as authentically Vietnamese, and Hyotteu has been a Blue Ribbon pick for several years. Tables are close together, but queues move fast.
tips: Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep); holidays otherwise run weekend hours without a break (Naver).
Register on the CatchTable waitlist as soon as it opens at the door.
Five minutes from Sinyongsan Station Exit 1 (Line 4); pair with Yongsan’s HYBE Insight or I’Park Mall.

reviews.text: TheSmartLocal describes authentic pho in a space that looks like a real Vietnamese street stall.
A diner notes tables are tight, but the hip atmosphere makes up for it — a true waiting-list hotspot.
Arriving when the on-site CatchTable list opened meant no wait; the fried eggplant with mint was a surprise hit.

summary: ₩10,000 spicy beef yukgaejang and bubbling nakgop hot pots in Banpo Shopping Town — the value lunch near home.
description: Ilbeonji Yukgaejang is a busy basement restaurant in Banpo Shopping Town by Express Bus Terminal Station, one stop from home. The fiery, shredded-beef yukgaejang costs ₩10,000, as do most stews, while groups share nakgop (octopus and beef intestine) or gopchang hot pots. Naver regulars praise the deep broth and generous portions — ideal after shopping at the terminal's underground mall.
tips: Hidden gem: 1,000+ Naver reviews; tourists shopping upstairs rarely find it.
Most stews are spicy — ask for less heat (덜 맵게) if parents prefer mild.
Open 24 Sep (11:00–22:30); closed 25–26 Sep per owner notice.
Express Bus Terminal Station Exit 8-2, 2 minutes; break 15:30–16:30.

summary: A 30-year Gyodae nopo for Eonyang-style grilled bulgogi, bossam sets and ₩10,000 beef-broth lunches.
description: Isim Jeonsim has served Gyodae for more than 30 years, best known for Eonyang bulgogi (finely chopped beef grilled flat) and bossam set meals. Lunch brings cheap, comforting bowls such as clear yangji-tang and tripe gukbap; in winter regulars come for fresh oysters and eoriguljeot. It is an old-school neighbourhood restaurant, a two-minute walk from Gyodae Station and very close to home.
tips: Hidden gem: a 30-year local nopo with 1,000+ Naver reviews and no English presence.
Lunch bowls from ₩10,000 are excellent value.

name: Jeongdon Gangnam
summary: Thick, juicy premium tonkatsu by Sinnonhyeon — a Seoul tonkatsu institution with a spacious, clean Gangnam branch.
description: Jeongdon made its name with thick-cut rosy tenderloin and loin katsu fried in a light, crackling crust, and the Gangnam branch is its roomiest location. Sets pair katsu with rice, miso and pickles, and there are black-tiger prawn katsu and zaru soba or udon tempura sets. Naver diners mention an instruction card explaining how to eat each cut, and several bring their parents. The room is bright and tidy, with enough tables for a group of five.
tips: Closed 24–25 Sep for Chuseok (Naver notice); reopens Sat 26.
Tenderloin sells out by evening — go at 11:30 opening or right after the 17:00 break.
3 minutes from Sinnonhyeon Station Exit 4 (Line 9 / Sinbundang); about 15 minutes from home by taxi.

reviews.text: A diner who brought their parents says tenderloin is a must, the black-tiger prawn is huge, and the parents loved it.
The meat is very thick yet tender, and the crust stays crisp to the last bite; sauces don’t overpower the pork.

name: Jin Jin
summary: Veteran chef Wang Yuk-sung’s Bib Gourmand Chinese kitchen: shrimp toast, crab-and-egg-white, mapo tofu to share.
description: Jin Jin was opened by chef Wang Yuk-sung, who has spent over 40 years popularising proper Chinese cooking in Korea, and deliberately keeps a short menu so every dish is consistent. It sits between Hapjeong and Hongdae and is listed by the Michelin Guide as a Bib Gourmand. The classics are menbosha (shrimp toast), stir-fried snow-crab meat with egg white, kkanpunggi and fish-fragrant eggplant. Portions are designed for sharing, which suits a family of five.
highlights: Stir-fried crab meat with egg white
tips: Order four or five plates to share; Naver diners suggest starting with crab-meat soup.

name: Jinokhwa Halmae Wonjo Dakhanmari
summary: The original Dongdaemun dakhanmari since 1978 — a whole chicken simmered at your table, then noodles in the broth.
description: Dakhanmari ('one whole chicken') was born in the alleys of Dongdaemun, and this three-storey restaurant claims the original recipe from 1978. A whole chicken arrives in a basin of broth with potatoes and rice cakes, simmering on a burner at your table; you dip pieces in a mix of chilli paste, soy, vinegar and mustard. Finish by adding kalguksu noodles to the rich broth. It is loud, fast, cheap and open until 1 am — perfect after Dongdaemun shopping.

tips: One chicken feeds about two to three; for five order two plus noodle sari.

reviews.text: As the heat fades, a regular returns each autumn for the rich broth and sauce; says tteok and noodle add-ons are a must (Sept 2026).

Gold-lit ceilings, red chairs and patterned marble make it one of the most design-forward buffet rooms in Seoul, and window tables look over Gangnam. Most dishes are cooked to order, from udon and xiaolongbao to grilled short-rib patties and shakshuka. Naver regulars rate the view, fruit and service highly.

description: Jungsik opened in 2009 and became the reference for modern Korean fine dining, later spawning Jungsik in New York. The multi-level Cheongdam building has private rooms for 2–10 guests, which suits a family of five. It holds two Michelin stars in 2026.

description: Kyodaiya (“brothers’ shop”) is run by two chef brothers who roll and cut Sanuki-style udon for every order, so the noodles keep their spring and gloss. description: Linus’ is a basement-level Alabama-style smokehouse down a stairway off Itaewon-ro, often called the best Southern BBQ in Seoul by TripAdvisor reviewers. Meats — brisket, spare ribs, pulled pork, smoked chicken — are served on metal trays with slider buns, fries, coleslaw and pickles. Family platters make it simple to feed five, and Naver diners describe the smell of smoke as you walk in. Wheat beer and IPAs round it out.

summary: Hongdae ramen-ya that feels like a Tokyo backstreet: rich tonkotsu, tsukemen and crisp-winged gyoza from ₩10,000.
description: Menya Sandaime has been a Hongdae ramen reference for over a decade, with a noren-hung wooden front and a small, Japanese-feeling room. name: Mongtan
summary: Straw-fire-seared beef short ribs grilled by staff in a converted old house by Samgakji — Seoul's most-queued BBQ.
description: Mongtan made its name with u-dae-galbi: thick bone-in beef short ribs seared over burning rice straw (jjipbul) downstairs, then finished at your table by staff. The building is a renovated older house near the War Memorial, with a bustling open grill room on the ground floor. Expect a smoky, fragrant, lively room rather than a quiet one. highlights: Yangpa bokkeumbap (onion fried rice) to finish

summary: Seoul's most famous kalguksu since 1966: rich chicken-broth noodles, thin-skinned dumplings and fiery garlic kimchi.
description: Myeongdong Kyoja has served the same short menu — kalguksu, mandu, bibim-guksu and summer kongguksu — since 1966, and Naver shows over 40,000 visitor reviews. name: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
summary: Seoul's giant live-seafood market: pick crab, fish and shellfish from the tanks, then eat it sliced or steamed upstairs.
description: Noryangjin is Seoul's main wholesale seafood market, now housed in a modern multi-level building beside Noryangjin Station. The ground floor is a sea of glowing tanks – king crab, snow crab, flounder, abalone, scallops, sea squirt – with vendors calling out prices. You buy by weight downstairs, the vendor cleans and slices it, and you carry it up to one of the 2nd-floor 'sangcharim' restaurants, which charge a per-person table fee and extra for steaming or for a spicy fish stew (maeuntang) made from the leftover frames. It is loud, wet-floored and brilliantly theatrical; the upstairs rooms are plain and functional rather than pretty.
highlights: Steamed king crab or snow crab (daege), with crab-butter fried rice made in the shell
Hoe (sliced raw fish) platter – flounder (gwang-eo) and rockfish (ureok)
Maeuntang – spicy stew made from the fish frames
Live scallops, abalone and prawns grilled or steamed upstairs
tips: Prices change daily and are per kg – check the TPirates (인어교주해적단) app for the day's going rate, agree the weight and total before anyone starts cleaning, and don't be shy to compare two or three stalls.
Upstairs restaurants charge a table-setting fee per person (e.g. Chungnam Sikdang lists ₩5,000 pp; maeuntang ₩10,000–15,000) plus steaming fees – ask the fee before sitting down.
Floors are wet and fishy downstairs; wear closed shoes. The building has parking and elevators, and upstairs restaurants take groups of 5 easily.
From home: Line 9 express from Express Bus Terminal reaches Noryangjin in about 10 minutes; use Line 9 Exit 7 or Line 1 Exit 9 and follow signs.

reviews.text: Travellers call it a seafood lover's paradise: choose live seafood downstairs and have it prepared upstairs for an extra fee.

description: Okdongsik reinvented dwaeji gukbap as a crystal-clear, gomtang-style broth made only from the legs of Jirisan black pigs. name: Onjium
summary: Royal-court and noble-household recipes reimagined, facing Gyeongbokgung's stone wall — Michelin one star.
description: Onjium is the restaurant of a research institute devoted to Korean heritage food, clothing and architecture. Its team studies Joseon-era court and aristocratic recipe books and turns them into precise seasonal tasting menus. The fourth-floor room is calm and minimal, looking across to the western wall of Gyeongbokgung Palace. It holds one Michelin star in 2026 and is one of Seoul's hardest reservations.
tips: Lunch ₩200,000 vs dinner ₩300,000; Korean-liquor pairing is cheaper than wine (Naver menu, 2026).

name: Oreno Ramen (Main)
summary: Michelin Bib Gourmand ramen in Hapjeong: creamy chicken paitan broth, blended to a froth, for about ₩13,000.
description: Oreno Ramen’s original Hapjeong shop has been a Michelin Bib Gourmand every year since 2019, according to Naver diners, and it is the city’s best-known tori paitan (chicken-bone) ramen. The broth is blitzed until frothy and served with chicken chashu, wood-ear mushrooms and a soft egg; the spicy kara paitan is the local favourite. Ordering is by kiosk and seating is mostly a counter plus small tables. Expect a line at peak meal times, but turnover is quick.
tips: Open through Chuseok with regular 11:00–22:00 hours on 24–26 Sep (Naver listing) — rare for a Hongdae-area favourite.
No break time: go around 14:30–16:30 on a weekday to skip the queue, as Naver diners recommend.
Choose coriander or kimchi at the kiosk; seats are mostly counter, so a group of five may be split.

reviews.text: A diner notes it has been a Michelin Bib Gourmand for eight straight years since 2019, explaining the long queues outside.

Travel guides describe a clean, less greasy chicken broth, with refills available on noodles, rice and broth.

name: Pierre Gagnaire à Séoul
summary: Pierre Gagnaire’s French restaurant on Lotte Hotel’s 35th floor: Murano chandeliers, gold trim and a sweep over Seoul.
description: Opened in 2008 atop the Lotte Hotel’s New Wing, this is the three-Michelin-star Parisian chef’s Seoul outpost, listed in the current Michelin Guide Seoul selection. The dining room is classic French luxury — Murano chandeliers, gold trim, orange velvet chairs — with windows over downtown and Namsan. Courses are multi-part and playful in Gagnaire’s style, using mostly local ingredients. TripAdvisor opinions are mixed on value, but Naver diners consistently praise the view, service and set-piece dishes.
tips: Lunch Déjeuner (₩180,000) gives the view at the lowest price; dinner courses are ₩280,000–320,000.

summary: Michelin Bib Pyongyang naengmyeon near Namsangol Hanok Village — clear, peppery broth and handmade mandu.
description: Pildong Myeonok belongs to the Uijeongbu school of Pyongyang cold noodles: a very clear, lightly peppery broth topped with chilli flakes and scallion, and firm buckwheat noodles. highlights: Bibim naengmyeon with sweet soy dressing

description: Pizzeria D’Buzza (Buzza Pizza) near Hangangjin has been reviewed by English-language Itaewon guides since at least 2013 and remains a Seoul favourite. Pizzas come from a wood-fired oven with leopard-spotted crusts — marinara, margherita con bufala, quattro formaggi, prosciutto e rucola — along with calzone salads and baked pasta. name: Pro Soy Crab (Sinsa main branch)
summary: Seoul's best-known soy-marinated raw crab house since 1980 – roe-packed female blue crab, 3 min from Sinsa Station.
description: Pro Soy Crab has served ganjang gejang – raw female blue crab cured in soy – on the same Sinsa corner since 1980, and now fills a multi-storey building with around 300 seats. The crab arrives cold and glossy, the shell full of orange roe; you squeeze the sweet flesh onto rice, then mix rice into the shell with the soy and wrap it in laver. The spicy yangnyeom version is sticky, sweet and garlicky, and the crab-roe bibimbap is a gentler option for anyone wary of raw seafood. It is busy, efficient and very used to international guests.
highlights: Ganjang gejang – soy-marinated female blue crab (2 crabs per order)
tips: For 5 people, one large ganjang + one large yangnyeom order plus a roe bibimbap covers a tasting; rice is extra (a reviewer paid ₩1,000 a bowl) and refills are expected.
Prices are high and in-store menus may not match Naver's listing (one July 2026 reviewer paid ₩136,000 for the extra-large two-crab order) – ask the price for each size when ordering.
Locals say order the gyeran-jjim (steamed egg) and skip the crab stew; the soy crab is the reason to come.
Exit 4 of Sinsa Station, 150 m then into the Starbucks side street; valet parking ₩4,000. Group seating is available on several floors.

reviews.text: An April 2026 visitor found the crab fresh with no fishy smell, and singled out the soft, silky steamed egg on the side.
Pricey, but reviewers say it is worth the visit and they did not regret spending the money.
Korean regulars say it is less salty than other gejang houses, with sweet, firm crab; several note it is now full of foreign visitors.
Critical locals complain the paper menu shows no prices and that valet parking is charged even though the restaurant owns the building.

name: Samarkand
summary: Uzbek canteen in Dongdaemun’s Central Asian quarter since 2003: tandoor shashlik, plov, lagman and manti.
description: Behind Dongdaemun History & Culture Park lies a small Central Asian quarter, and Samarkand has served Uzbek home cooking there since 2003, according to Visit Seoul. Lamb shashlik is grilled over fire, plov rice is glossy with meat stock, and hand-pulled lagman, manti dumplings, shurpa and borscht fill the menu. Naver diners say the interior feels like being in Uzbekistan and flavours are mild enough for anyone. Almost no Western tourists find it.
tips: Open through Chuseok 09:00–23:00 on 24–27 Sep (Naver).
Closed on alternate Tuesdays — call before going on 29 Sep.

name: Samwon Garden
summary: Apgujeong's big galbi house since 1976: marinated short ribs grilled by staff, beside a landscaped garden
description: Samwon Garden has served marinated galbi (short ribs) in Apgujeong since 1976, and it reopened in 2022 after a full rebuild. The new building has high ceilings and glass walls onto a landscaped garden, which makes the large hall bright and calm even when it is full. Staff grill the beef at the table, from the signature soy-marinated galbi to hanwoo sirloin and special cuts. There is also a long list of dishes for people who don't want meat, such as naengmyeon, galbi-tang and ganjang-gejang (soy-marinated crab). The MICHELIN Guide lists it as a Selected restaurant for 2026, recommended for groups.
highlights: Weekday lunch set with hanwoo bulgogi (₩55,000)
Naengmyeon to finish (a ₩11,000 taster portion is on the menu)
tips: The weekday-only lunch set costs ₩55,000 per person (minimum two people). You choose hanwoo bulgogi, soy crab or barley-dried croaker, with naengmyeon or doenjang stew, which makes it the good-value way in.
Private rooms seat groups. Book one for five on CatchTable, especially for dinner and weekends.
Order a small taster naengmyeon (맛보기 냉면) after the galbi, as Korean regulars do. Parking is easy, and on Naver it is often praised as roomy and clean.
Apgujeong Station (Line 3) Exit 3 is about an 8-minute walk. The break is 14:30–17:30 on weekdays and 14:30–17:00 at weekends.

summary: One of Seoul's 'top three' jokbal: glossy, chewy trotters in an old-school Seongsu shop locals queue for.
description: Seongsu Jokbal has been braising trotters in the old factory district since the 1980s and is routinely named among Seoul's three best jokbal. summary: Yannick Alléno’s modern French restaurant on Lotte World Tower’s 81st floor — sky-high Han River views with every course.
description: STAY sits on the 81st floor of Lotte World Tower inside the Signiel hotel, with a black-and-white checkerboard floor, gold pendant lights and full-height windows over the Han River and Jamsil. STAY Fun (₩135,000) is the entry course; pair with Seoul Sky or Lotte World Mall.

name: Soonhee's Bindaetteok (Gwangjang Market)
summary: Gwangjang Market's most famous bindaetteok: mung beans stone-ground and fried crisp in front of you, ₩6,000 each.
description: Soonhee's has fried bindaetteok in Gwangjang Market for about 40 years. Mung beans are ground on a millstone at the front, mixed with pork, kimchi and bean sprouts, and deep-pan-fried into thick, crunchy-edged pancakes. Seating is simple and crowded inside the market, so treat it as a lively snack stop rather than a long meal. Naver visitors most often praise the taste and value.
tips: Share one pancake per two people and keep room for other stalls.
Seating is tight benches — fine for a short stop; older parents may prefer to take it away.
Bring some cash just in case; older guides describe it as cash-only.
Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep) only.

reviews.text: A 15-year regular says each visit shows how much Korea's global profile has risen — the market is full of visitors (Aug 2026).
Took Mum on a date; she loved the thick mung-bean pancake (Aug 2026).
Visit Seoul notes they grind mung beans on a millstone and fry on the spot for a crispy, savoury pancake.

name: Soseoul Hannam
summary: Michelin-star modern Seoul cuisine in a sleek Hannam basement — kelp chips, aged kimchi, chargrilled webfoot octopus.

summary: Hannam’s sunny Aussie brunch café: smashed avo, croissant French toast and flat whites under yellow awnings.
description: Summer Lane brings an Australian all-day brunch to a Hannam side street, with yellow awnings, beach murals and pastel tables. name: Sushi Ryeo Premium
summary: Counter sushi omakase in Seocho-dong, 10 minutes from home: generous ₩75,000 lunch course from a meticulous master chef.
description: Sushi Ryeo Premium is a calm, light-wood omakase counter on the second floor of the Acrotel building near Gangnam Station Exit 5 — one of the closest serious sushi counters to home. The course moves from clear dashi soup and seasonal small plates (sweet prawn, simmered fish) to a long run of nigiri and a sea-urchin hand roll. Naver regulars say the lunch omakase is unusually filling for the price and single out the chef’s consistent, precise shaping. Few foreign visitors know it.
highlights: Seasonal small plates and clear soup
tips: Open daily 11:40–21:30 (break 14:40–18:30); no Chuseok closure listed on Naver, but confirm when booking.
Counter seating — book five seats together for lunch.

name: Thai Elephant
summary: Gangnam Station basement Thai with bamboo lanterns and street-market décor: tom yum hot pot, curries, som tam and leng saeb.
description: Thai Elephant sits in a basement off Gangnam-daero, decorated with bamboo lanterns, Thai posters and a small bar. The menu covers pad thai with prawns, curries, stir-fried morning glory, green papaya som tam, a bubbling tom yum hot pot and leng saeb (spicy pork-spine soup). Naver diners rate it near-perfect for local flavour and interior, while noting some dishes are adapted for Korean palates. It is a short ride from home and good for a relaxed group dinner.
tips: Open 24 Sep 10:00–20:00; closed 25–26 Sep and every Sunday (Naver).
Five minutes from Gangnam Station — about 15 minutes from home.
Order a hot pot plus 3–4 dishes for five people.

reviews.text: A self-described Thai-food fanatic ranks the morning glory in their personal top three — just wishes portions were bigger.

name: Tosokchon Samgyetang
summary: Seoul's famous ginseng-chicken soup in a rambling hanok near Gyeongbokgung — nutty, thick broth and fast queues.
description: Tosokchon is the samgyetang house every guidebook mentions, and it is still packed with Koreans as well as visitors. A whole young chicken stuffed with glutinous rice, ginseng and jujube arrives bubbling in a thick, nutty broth made with ground grains and seeds. The restaurant spreads through several connected hanok rooms, so big groups are seated quickly. It is a short walk from Gyeongbokgung Station — ideal after the palace.
tips: The line looks long but moves quickly — the hanok has many rooms.
Open 10:00–22:00 daily; go before 11:30 or after 14:00.

summary: Hugely popular Spanish restaurant near Yeoksam: paella, gambas and Ibérico steak in easy set menus for groups.
description: Traga is one of Seoul’s most-reviewed Spanish restaurants, with thousands of Naver visitor reviews for its Yeoksam branch. tips: The three-person premium set (₩129,000) plus one extra paella feeds five.

description: Ttin Ttin fills a basement corner of SFC Mall, steps from Gwanghwamun and City Hall stations, with a jungle-green, lantern-lit room. summary: Korea’s first Wolfgang’s: sizzling dry-aged USDA Prime porterhouse carved tableside in a big, polished Cheongdam room.
description: Founded by a 40-year Peter Luger veteran, Wolfgang’s opened its first Korean branch in Cheongdam, and it remains the city’s benchmark New York–style steakhouse. USDA Prime beef is dry-aged in-house for 22–28 days, broiled and served sizzling in butter, carved at the table. The brick building has plenty of space for groups, and Naver shows over 10,000 visitor reviews praising the steak, service and celebratory feel. TripAdvisor scores are more modest (3.9), with some diners citing price.
highlights: Porterhouse for two or more (1 kg ₩370,000)
tips: The lunch course (₩130,000) is the value way in; book CatchTable early — slots can close early when fully reserved.

name: Woo Lae Oak
summary: Since 1946: the benchmark Pyongyang cold noodles in hanwoo broth, plus old-school bulgogi — a Michelin Bib Seoul legend.
description: Woo Lae Oak has served Pyongyang-style naengmyeon in Euljiro since 1946, and many Seoulites still consider it the reference bowl. The broth is simmered from hanwoo shank and seasoned only with salt and soy, so it tastes clean and beefy rather than sweet. Big, bright dining halls over two floors take families easily, and bulgogi grilled at the table makes a classic pairing. It is listed as a Bib Gourmand in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul 2026.
tips: Weekend waits of 1.5–2.5 hours were reported in Aug 2026 — register at the door and explore Gwangjang Market or Cheonggyecheon while you wait.
Weekdays have a 14:00–17:00 break; arrive at 11:30 or just before 17:00.
Closed Mondays and across Chuseok (24–26 Sep).
Valet parking available; Euljiro 4-ga Station Exit 4 is 2 minutes away.

name: Yakitori Mook
summary: Charcoal yakitori omakase in Yeonnam from chef Kim Byoung-mook, the “yakitori king” of Netflix’s Culinary Class Wars.
description: Chef Kim Byoung-mook grills free-range chicken over binchotan and straw along a long open counter, working through thigh, heart, skin and tsukune with a poached egg. The Michelin Guide Seoul lists the restaurant, and his run on Netflix’s Culinary Class Wars made seats harder to get. Naver diners call the omakase juicy and good value for the quality, though one found a recent visit over-salted. There is also a newer Sinsa branch closer to home.
tips: Dinner only, 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:00); book on CatchTable.
One drink per person (or one bottle per table) is required; corkage ₩30,000 per wine/sake bottle.
Counter seating — ask for five seats together, or try the Sinsa branch.

name: Yeongdong Seolleongtang
summary: Milky ox-bone seolleongtang served almost round the clock by Sinsa Station for 30+ years — Gangnam's classic late meal.
description: Yeongdong Seolleongtang has fed Gangnam night owls for decades from a corner near Sinsa Station, three stops from home on Line 3. The menu is essentially one soup — rich, milky ox-bone broth with thin slices of beef and noodles — plus suyuk for sharing, and rice or broth refills are free. It is open around the clock apart from a 15:00–17:00 break, recently renovated, and has its own parking lot.
tips: Season it yourself with salt, scallion and pepper at the table; ask for extra noodles.
Open 24 hours except a 15:00–17:00 break — perfect after a late night in Sinsa or Garosu-gil.

name: Yu Yuan (Four Seasons Seoul)
summary: Michelin-starred Cantonese room at the Four Seasons: carved Peking duck, dim sum lunches and 1920s-Shanghai glamour.
description: Yu Yuan on the Four Seasons’ 11th floor channels 1920s Shanghai with teal walls, brass screens and lamp-lit tables. tips: Lunch Delights course (₩140,000) is the gentlest entry; dinner courses run ₩280,000–320,000.
Order the Peking duck in advance when booking.

name: Cafe Onion Anguk
summary: A restored hanok turned bakery café: floor cushions, tiled courtyard and the snow-capped pandoro that made Onion famous
description: Onion Anguk sits in a restored hanok a few steps from Anguk Station Exit 3, with seating on wooden maru floors around a tiled courtyard. summary: A cavernous old warehouse turned gallery café — trees, sculptures and firewood-lined walls in Seongsu
description: Daelim Changgo is the converted warehouse that defined Seongsu's factory-café style: soaring ceilings, big installations and paintings, and long timber tables with room for any group. name: Suyeon Sanbang
summary: Tea in novelist Lee Tae-jun's 1930s hanok home in Seongbuk-dong — jujube tea and pumpkin bingsu in a secret garden
description: Suyeon Sanbang is the former house of short-story writer Sangheo Lee Tae-jun, who lived here from 1933 to 1946; it is now a tea house in the hills of Seongbuk-dong. Guests sit on the maru or in the small garden with jujube ssanghwa tea (15,500원) or the famous pumpkin bingsu and red-bean porridge. Naver reviewers call it especially atmospheric on rainy days; they also note it is small, the chairs are not built for long stays and prices are high.

Pair with Gilsangsa temple (10 min walk) for a quiet half-day.

summary: Seoul’s oldest bakery (1946): retro hall, butter bread and the legendary milk monaka ice cream

summary: Korea's oldest jazz club (since 1976), now in a dramatic all-red Itaewon room with live bands every night of the week.
description: All That Jazz opened in Itaewon in 1976 and is the country's oldest active jazz club; in 2023 it moved into a 275 m² second-floor space on Itaewon-ro designed by studio mttb, reached through a red door and a neon-lit corridor. The room is wrapped in red curtains and banquettes, with a long bar and a proper stage for piano, horns and big bands. There are two sets on weeknights (19:00–20:00 and 20:30–23:00) and three on Fridays and Saturdays, the last running until 02:50. The music charge is ₩15,000 per person per set, paid on the night, on top of cocktails, wine and plates.
highlights: Live jazz 364 days a year, with a new line-up nightly
Red, cinematic 2023 interior by mttb, with a long cocktail bar
Fri/Sat three-set nights; bands and quintets in the early set
tips: Cover is ₩15,000 per person per set (two sets = ₩30,000); it is charged on the night, not when you book.
For 5 people incl. parents, book a table in advance on the club's website or Kakao channel and go for the 19:00 or 20:30 set; weeknights are calmer and walk-ins usually work for couples.
Naver reviewers suggest window seats, and eating dinner elsewhere first — drinks are the strength here.
No building parking; valet is reported at the nearby IBK bank branch. Itaewon Stn (Line 6) Exit 3 is about a 6-minute walk.

name: Bar 81 (Signiel Seoul)
summary: Champagne sky bar on the 81st floor of Lotte World Tower: floor-to-ceiling windows over the Han River and all of Seoul.
description: Bar 81 sits inside Signiel Seoul on the 81st floor of Lotte World Tower, Korea's tallest building, so the view out of the full-height windows takes in the Han River bridges on one side and the Jamsil/Gangnam skyline on the other. The room is dark and dramatic, with a double-height ceiling hung with a cloud of glass 'champagne bubbles' and a long marble bar. It is known for one of Asia's largest champagne lists, plus classic and signature cocktails and French-style snack plates (cheese, charcuterie). Forbes Travel Guide named it among the world's best hotel sky bars in 2019. On Friday and Saturday nights a DJ plays, and reviewers report a per-person entrance charge on weekends.
highlights: Window table at sunset, then the lights-on night view (roughly 18:00–20:00 in late September)
Champagne by the glass from a very deep list
Signature cocktails with a cheese or charcuterie plate
Friday–Saturday DJ set 21:30–23:15 (per a Jan 2026 visitor report)
tips: Book a window table in advance (CatchTable or +82-2-3213-1281); a Jan 2026 visitor says window seats are fought over and weekend walk-ins are hard. Online booking slots run 17:00–21:00.

Money flags: a Jan 2026 blog reports a weekend entrance charge of about ₩31,000 per person, and one TripAdvisor reviewer (Oct 2023) says staff asked every member of their group to order. Assume everyone orders at least one drink.
Dress smart casual (no gym wear or flip-flops). The bar has its own smoking room, so the main room stays smoke-free.
Enter at the Signiel lobby entrance at the base of Lotte World Tower (not the Seoul Sky observatory queue) and take the hotel lift up. Pair it with dinner in Lotte World Mall below.

name: Bar Cham
summary: Hanok cocktail bar in Seochon built on Korean spirits and soju; No. 33 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026.
description: Bar Cham sits in a renovated hanok (traditional house) in Seochon, with oak beams and hand-built furniture. Staff guide you through traditional Korean spirits (jeontongju) from across the country, and the cocktails are built on soju and local liquors. It placed No. 33 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026. The room is calm rather than loud, and it is often cited as one of the most distinctly Korean bars in the city.
highlights: Cocktails built on Korean traditional liquors and soju
Knowledgeable staff who explain each spirit
tips: Party-size rule: TripAdvisor reviewers report a strict maximum of 4 per group, so a family of 5 should split into 2 + 3 or expect to be refused.
Waits are long. Arrive at the 18:00 opening or put your name down early and have dinner nearby in Seochon.
Closed Tuesdays. Pair it with a Gyeongbokgung palace afternoon; it is 6 min from Gyeongbokgung Stn Exit 2 (Line 3, direct from home).

reviews.text: Reviewers praise the original Korean-spirit recipes, fun staff and wonderful vibe, while noting the drinks are a little pricey.

name: Charles H.
summary: Prohibition-style speakeasy hidden in the Four Seasons Seoul basement; No. 87 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026.
description: Charles H. is tucked behind an unmarked door on the lower level of the Four Seasons Hotel Seoul, off Gwanghwamun. It takes its name and spirit from the 1920s travelling bartender Charles H. Baker: a plush Prohibition-era lounge with a menu inspired by his global travels. Hotel-grade service, sofa seating, valet parking and a group-friendly flag on Naver make it one of the easiest world-class bars for a family of 5.

name: Club Evans
summary: Hongdae's 25-year-old jazz club: two live sets nightly a few steps from the stage, for about ₩15,000–20,000 entry.
description: Club Evans, named after pianist Bill Evans, has been the home stage of Korea's young jazz scene near Hongik University since 2001 and runs its own label. There is no barrier between stage and tables, so you sit a few metres from the players. Doors open at 19:00, the first set runs 20:00–20:50 and the second 21:20–22:10, with a different band every night and open jam sessions on Mondays and Tuesdays. Entry is ₩15,000 Sunday–Friday and ₩20,000 on Saturday, plus one drink per person; cocktails and beer are simple and inexpensive.
highlights: A different Korean jazz band every night, often the scene's best young players
Open jam nights on Mondays ('Super Jam Day') and Tuesdays ('Urban Jam Day')
Intimate room with no barrier between stage and tables
Blue Lagoon and other classic cocktails at bar-snack prices
tips: No reservations — seats are first come, first served. On weekends a queue forms, so arrive at 19:00 when doors open if you want a table for 5; back rows are cramped.
Budget ₩15,000 entry (₩20,000 on Saturday) plus one compulsory drink each; the fee can change for special shows.
It is a small, second-floor room (entrance to the right of the 7-Eleven, 150 m from Sangsu Stn Exit 1). Parents who dislike tight seating may prefer All That Jazz.
Under-19s are admitted only with a legal guardian.

summary: Near-home jeon-and-traditional-liquor pub under Banpo Shopping Town: Korean pancakes, makgeolli and a big sool list.
description: Dameun is a basement yori-jujeom (Korean gastro-pub) in Banpo Shopping Town, right at Express Bus Terminal Station. It is one Line 3 stop from home. name: Euljiro Nogari Alley (Manseon Hof)
summary: Legendary Euljiro alley of plastic tables, cheap draft beer and grilled nogari (dried pollack), anchored by Manseon Hof since 1980.
description: Around Euljiro 3-ga's printing-shop lanes, hofs spill hundreds of plastic tables onto the street every evening. Crowds drink cold draft beer here with grilled nogari (dried young pollack) dipped in spicy sauce and mayo. Manseon Hof, running since 1980, started the trend and now spreads across several buildings, including rooftop sections. It is the most 'real Seoul' night out on this list: loud, cheap, very Korean, and easy for a group of 5 to grab a table. Naver reviewers rate it highly for value (394 mentions) and for group gatherings.
highlights: Grilled nogari with spicy mayo dip
Golbaengi muchim (spicy sea-snail salad with noodles)
Outdoor street tables on warm September evenings
tips: Go 18:00–19:00 to get an outdoor table before the after-work crowd; by 20:00 on Thu–Fri the alley is packed.
Order a round of draft beer and nogari first, since both come fast and cheap, then add chicken or golbaengi.
Rain plan: Manseon Hof spreads over several buildings with indoor seating, so the night still works.
Euljiro 3-ga Stn Exit 4 (Line 2/3) is 3 min away. It is a direct Line 3 ride from Nambu Bus Terminal.

reviews.text: Naver visitors praise the food, the value for money (394 mentions) and how good it is for group gatherings.

price.note: Among the cheapest nights out in central Seoul: draft beer plus shared snacks

description: Hanchu is a single-location hof near Garosu-gil that has fried chicken for over 20 years; it is not a franchise. summary: Seongsu gastro-pub pairing Korea's traditional liquors with modern anju such as octopus bossam and beef tartare.
description: Haneum is a modern yori-jujeom a minute from Ttukseom Station, popular with Seongsu's young crowd for its menu of Korean traditional liquors. The anju (drinking food) is serious: garlic octopus bossam, sushi-style hot pots, yukhoe (beef tartare) and seafood-and-chive jeon. It has over 1,200 Naver visitor reviews, with more than a thousand praising the food and 552 the drink range. It accepts reservations and group tables, so it is a comfortable way for parents to try sool beyond soju.
tips: Closed Sat 26 Sep (Chuseok) and every Sunday. Open 24 and 25 Sep.
Pair it with an afternoon at Seoul Forest or the Seongsu pop-ups; Ttukseom Stn Exit 7 or 8 is 1–2 min away.
Ask staff for a tasting-style mix of takju (makgeolli) and yakju (clear rice wine) to share among 5.

reviews.text: Naver visitors overwhelmingly praise the food (1,104 mentions) and the drink variety, and say the room is good for conversation.
Reviewers also mention generous complimentary side dishes and an attractive interior.

hours.note: Closed Sundays

chuseok.note: Open Thu 24 and Fri 25 Sep (17:00–02:00); closed Sat 26 Sep for Chuseok and Sun 27 (regular day off).

name: Jusindang (Zoo Sindang) Gangnam
summary: Shaman-shrine themed bar with a cocktail for each of the 12 Korean zodiac animals, 3 min from Gangnam Station.
description: Jusindang (酒神堂, 'house of the god of drink') turns Korean shamanic imagery into a moody, design-forward bar. The menu has one cocktail for each of the 12 zodiac animals (rat, ox, tiger and so on), so each family member can order their own birth-year drink. Unlike most cocktail bars, the Gangnam branch runs a proper Korean-modern kitchen: grilled hanwoo steak, sous-vide beef short rib, spicy fish stew and potato jeon. With 9,500 Naver visitor reviews, it is a Seoul favourite with locals yet little known to tourists.
highlights: Potato jeon and gondre noodles for sharing
Lunch and evening set courses from ₩18,000
tips: Look up each person's Korean zodiac animal by birth year before you go; it is a fun ritual to order by sign.
Opens 11:00 with a 15:00–17:00 break, so a lunch course here is an easy daytime taste of the concept for parents.
Naver lists reservations and a high chair for this branch. Book for 5 on weekends, when the Gangnam queue gets long.
Gangnam Stn Exit 11 (Line 2 / Shinbundang), 3 min walk. It is 2 stops from Gyodae on Line 2.

reviews.text: Naver visitors praise the food (7,812 mentions) as much as the drinks, and 5,665 highlight the striking interior.
The Smart Local describes a hidden oriental bar where you order a cocktail matched to your zodiac sign, entered past a stone guardian statue.
A 2025 review calls it part bar, part themed experience: modern design built around a contemporary take on Korean shamanism.

hours.note: Daily, with a break from 15:00 to 17:00

name: Kkokkio Firewood Chicken
summary: Two-floor Gangnam pub for firewood-roasted chicken, golbaengi and nogari with soju or beer; open until 03:30.
description: Kkokkio is a big, busy Gangnam Station pub built around whole chicken roasted over firewood. The house special is hanbang nurungji tongdak: herbal chicken on crispy scorched rice. Around it sit the classic Korean drinking anju: spicy golbaengi with noodles, fire-grilled boneless chicken feet, nogari and meoktae (dried pollack), and pojangmacha udon. At ₩19,900 for the signature chicken, it is solid value for Gangnam. Naver visitors praise the food (1,222 mentions) and the roomy two floors (527).

Golbaengi somyeon (spicy sea snails with noodles)
Nogari and meoktae with mayo dip
tips: Open daily 16:00–03:30 (last order 02:30), so it is a safe late-night fallback.
Two floors with group tables; Naver also lists high chairs.
5 min from Gangnam Stn Exit 3.

reviews.text: Naver visitors mostly praise the food, how spacious it is and the fresh ingredients.
Reviewers point to the signature scorched-rice roast chicken as the reason to go.

name: Koya Record
summary: Euljiro back-alley music bar loved for its vinyl sound, drinks and food; opens at noon on weekends.
description: Koya Record hides in the back lane behind J-Macro Tower in Euljiro, reached through a side door by a real-estate office sign. It is larger than most LP bars, marked group-friendly and bookable, so it suits a group of 5. From Friday to Sunday it opens at noon, which is rare for a music bar.
highlights: Food menu that works as dinner
tips: Naver lists it as a no-kids zone, so it is adults only. Book a table for 5 on Naver.
Finding it: go to the back alley of J-Macro Tower 1F and enter via the door to the right of the real-estate sign.
Pairs well with Euljiro nogari alley (5 min away) for a two-stop Euljiro night.

reviews.text: Naver visitors praise the music most (710 mentions), closely followed by the drink list, interior and food.

name: Le Chamber
summary: Gentlemen's-club speakeasy behind a bookshelf in Cheongdam; No. 88 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 and open till 03:00–04:00.
description: Le Chamber hides behind a bookcase: pull the right book and the wall opens onto a basement lounge of couches, a long marble bar and suited bartenders. It is one of Cheongdam's original high-end speakeasies, with a big whisky and champagne list alongside classic and signature cocktails. It placed No. 88 on the 2026 Asia's 50 Best Bars 51–100 list. It stays open very late, until 04:00 on Fridays and Saturdays.
highlights: Open till 04:00 on Fri and Sat
tips: There is a per-person cover charge, as noted by TripAdvisor reviewers. Weekends are packed.
Book a sofa section for 5 rather than bar seats.
Across the street from Alice, so you can pair the two in one night. 2 min from Apgujeong Rodeo Stn Exit 4.

Naver visitors praise the wide drink selection, handsome interior and signature menu.

summary: Design-led Sinsa basement wine bar with a huge list and good music; very limited opening days during the trip.
description: Liquortation is a basement wine bar in the Nonfiction building between Sinsa and Apgujeong. name: Magpie Brewshop Itaewon
summary: Original taproom of Magpie, the Itaewon brewery that helped start Korea's craft-beer boom, pouring fresh Jeju-brewed drafts.
description: Magpie Brewing was founded in Itaewon's Gyeongnidan in 2012 by four beer-loving friends and helped spark Korea's craft-beer revolution. The Brewshop keeps the original concept: just great beer, with fresh drafts shipped from Magpie's brewery on Jeju. There is no kitchen, but you can bring food or order delivery. It is small and casual, rated 4.5 on TripAdvisor, and good value for a beer-lover's hour before dinner in Itaewon or Haebangchon.
highlights: Magpie Pale Ale, Porter and IPA on draft
tips: Open Wed–Sun 17:00–23:00 only; closed Mon, Tue and Chuseok day (25 Sep).
The entrance is in the first alley on the left off the main road.
Small room: treat it as a first-round beer, then move on to dinner.

reviews.text: Reviewers call it a craft-beer pioneer with excellent fresh drafts and a friendly, low-key crowd.

name: M+MS
summary: Café by day, experimental fermentation cocktail bar by night; new at No. 42 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026.
description: M+MS is the newcomer of the 2026 list, entering Asia's 50 Best Bars at No. 42. It runs as a café in the afternoon, then turns into a cocktail bar with its own in-house brewing and fermentation programme. The drinks are deliberately experimental; the list's write-up singles out Yama, made with sour kimchi and tuna. Naver reviewers call it the most-talked-about bar in Apgujeong right now, and it has a perfect 5.0 visitor score there.
highlights: Experimental signature drinks such as the kimchi-and-tuna Yama
Opens at 14:00, so it works as an afternoon stop
tips: The 14:00 opening makes it one of the few Asia's 50 Best bars you can visit in daylight, which suits parents who prefer an early evening.
No valet parking: use the public lot on Dosan-daero 45-gil. It is 7 min from Apgujeong Rodeo Stn Exit 5.
Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep).

reviews.text: Korea Herald notes it works as a café in the afternoon and a cocktail bar in the evening, with an in-house brewery and fermentation programme.
A Naver reviewer calls it the most-watched bar in Apgujeong right now. Very experimental cocktails with a different feel from the other ranked bars.

name: MOBO Bar (JW Marriott Hotel Seoul)
subcategory: Hotel botanical cocktail bar with garden terrace
summary: A 'modern botanical' cocktail bar on JW Marriott Banpo's 7th floor, with its own greenhouse and garden terrace, two Line 3 stops from home.
description: MOBO (short for 'modern botanical') is on the 7th floor of JW Marriott Hotel Seoul, above Express Bus Terminal and the Shinsegae Gangnam complex. A long dark-wood bar faces a wall of grow-lit shelves. Behind it are a glass greenhouse where the team grows herbs and fruit for the drinks, and an open-air garden terrace with sofas. The cocktail list is built around five themes (Tonic, Fruits, Herbs, Spices and Earth). In 2025 Forbes Travel Guide put it on its 58 Star Bars list, the only bar in Korea to make it. It is TripAdvisor's top-rated hotel bar in this group and the closest to home.
highlights: Garden terrace on a mild late-September evening
Herb-forward signature cocktails such as Herb of Grace (₩29,000) and San Martini (₩38,000)
Forbes Travel Guide 2025 Star Bar (only one in Korea)
tips: The easiest nightcap from home: two stops on Line 3 to Express Bus Terminal, or a short taxi. It stays open until 02:00 on Friday and Saturday.
Ask for the outdoor terrace sofas for 5. Naver reviewers single out the outdoor space (야외공간이 멋져요), and the terrace suits parents better than bar stools.
Marriott's listing marks it as not taking reservations, so arrive early on Friday and Saturday or phone +82-2-6282-6739 to check.
Hotel parking at JW Marriott is free for 5 hours, per Naver.

tripadvisor.rank: #14 of 23,675 Restaurants in Seoul

reviews.text: Cozy bar with good food & drinks and, above all, great service.
reviews.author: Peter

reviews.text: The atmosphere is very good and the cocktails are fresh and delicious.
Korean visitors praise the outdoor terrace atmosphere, the bartenders' skill and the service, while noting that prices are hotel-level.
On Naver, visitors most often vote for tasty food, kind staff, a wide drinks list, the interior and the outdoor space.

price.note: Per cocktail: Summer Spritz ₩28,000, Herb of Grace ₩29,000, San Martini ₩38,000; Glen Grant 12 ₩31,000 (DiningCode menu listing). Expect about ₩40,000+ per person once snacks are added.

name: Monday Blues
summary: Seocho-side wine bistro near Gangnam Station: 72-hour pork belly, sirloin steak and paella with a friendly wine list.
description: Monday Blues is a wine bar and bistro on the Seocho side of Gangnam Station, in the lobby of the Samsung Chervill building. It is serious about food: 72-hour slow-cooked pork belly, sirloin steak, crab rosé pasta and squid-ink paella, all built for sharing with a bottle. Naver visitors praise the food first (646 mentions) and the interior second, with 1,155 blog reviews. It opens at 11:00 for lunch, which makes an early family dinner easy, and it is about 15 minutes from home.
tips: Holiday schedule on Naver: open 24 and 26 Sep (11:00–23:00 with a 15:00–17:00 break), closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep).
Gangnam Stn Exit 5 (Shinbundang) is 2 min away. Turn right at the Samsung Fire alley; it is in the building lobby by Kkanbu Chicken.
Book a table for 5 on Naver; it is group-friendly and has parking.

reviews.text: Naver visitors praise the food above all (646 mentions), then the interior and a room that is good for talking.
Reviewers highlight distinctive dishes and friendly staff.

price.note: Shared plates plus wine by the bottle

name: Mood Seoul (Some Sevit)
summary: Wine bar on Some Sevit's floating Solbit island, near home, with Han River night views by Banpo Bridge.
description: Mood Seoul occupies Solbit, one of the Some Sevit floating islands on the Han River beside Banpo Bridge. It is the closest real riverside night-view bar to home. The wine list comes with a full kitchen; the signature is pomodoro pasta topped with lobster, snow crab, octopus, abalone and shrimp. Naver visitors rate the interior highest (377 mentions), then the food. With the water all around and the city lit up across the river, it is a comfortable, parent-friendly way to do 'Seoul at night'.
highlights: Han River and Banpo Bridge views from a floating island
Wine by the glass and bottle
tips: Closed Thu 24 Sep for Chuseok; open 25 and 26 Sep. Weekday kitchen closes early (last order 20:30), so book 18:00–19:00.
Getting there: Express Bus Terminal Stn Exit 4 then bus 740 one stop, or a 20-min walk from Exit 8-1. A taxi from home is quickest.
Walk the Banpo Hangang Park riverside afterwards; the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain is on Banpo Bridge right next door (check the day's show times).

reviews.text: Naver visitors rate the interior and setting highest, followed by the food and friendly service.
The seafood pomodoro pasta with lobster and snow crab is the dish most visitors order.

price.note: Wine and dining; seafood pasta is the signature

name: The Paris Bar (Grand Hyatt Seoul)
summary: Grand Hyatt's French-styled bar on Namsan, with live jazz, signature cocktails and Seoul city lights beyond the windows.

For parents it is the most classic, comfortable way to enjoy a night view: armchairs, valet parking and five-star service.

City-light views from the Namsan hillside
Signature cocktails and French-inspired bar snacks

Reserve a window table on TableCheck.
No subway nearby (Hannam-jin Stn is a 20-min uphill walk). Take a taxi, or use valet if driving.

reviews.text: Naver visitors mostly praise the music, kind staff, drink range and a clean, stylish room.
Hotel listings describe a classy, discreet bar with French elements and spectacular views of the capital.

name: Pyeonggyunyul
summary: Dimly lit Euljiro LP bar with shelves of vinyl, wine and whisky; request a record from the jazz-heavy collection.
description: Pyeonggyunyul is a dim second-floor LP bar right by Euljiro 3-ga Station. Walls of vinyl surround the room, and staff spin jazz and classics, taking song requests (Chet Baker is a house favourite). Guests come for wine and whisky rather than cocktails, and for the romance of the room. Naver visitors rate the music first (185 mentions), then the interior; its 893 blog reviews make it one of the best-known LP bars among young Koreans.
highlights: Wine and whisky by the glass
tips: Naver lists it as a no-kids zone, so it is adults only. The room is intimate, so a group of 5 should book.
Opens 13:00 on Saturdays (break 17:00–18:00) and 14:00 on Sundays, making it a great rainy-afternoon stop.
Euljiro 3-ga Stn Exit 8 is directly below (Line 3 from home). Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep).

reviews.text: Trazy describes a jazzy LP bar where you drink whisky or wine beside shelves of records and can request songs.
Budify calls it a place of darkness and romance: a wine LP bar that turns nostalgic tracks and good wine into joy.
Naver visitors most often praise the music and the atmospheric interior.

name: Saeseoul
summary: Pink building with a retro arcade downstairs, a Korean-twist cocktail bar and a rooftop over the Jongno 3-ga hanok roofs.
description: Saeseoul stacks a retro game arcade on the lower floors, a cocktail bar on the third and a rooftop terrace looking over the low hanok roofs of Ikseon-dong and Jongno. Cocktails come with alcohol, sweetness and acidity ratings on the menu, and several are named after arcade games, such as Pac-Man. It sits right at the mouth of the Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha street, where orange-tented street stalls set up every evening. With over 5,600 Naver visitor reviews, it is hugely popular with young Seoulites but rarely on tourist lists.
highlights: Rooftop views over Ikseon-dong hanok roofs
Retro arcade games on the way up
Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha tent street right outside
tips: Naver lists it as a no-kids zone, which is fine for adults. Book the rooftop for groups on Naver.
Blankets are provided on cool evenings, and late-September nights can be chilly up top.
Combine it with the orange-tent pojangmacha stalls on the street outside for an easy two-stop night.
Jongno 3-ga Stn Exit 4 is 2 min away. Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep).

reviews.text: Over 2,700 Naver visitors single out the view, alongside the drink range and good food.
Travellers note you walk through the arcade and up several floors to find it; the vibe shifts from relaxed afternoon to DJ-led lounge at night.
